subject: Acme - Pricing & Invoice Estimate
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <p.natarajan@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Acme - Pricing & Invoice Estimate

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Great to meet you on the call earlier — appreciate the context on your search/replace workflow and the expected peak latency targets. Quick recap and a rough cost model attached so you have something to share with procurement: attached is acme_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx (input your monthly token volumes and the sheet will auto-populate the unit economics).

Recap of what we discussed:
- Workload: mixed chat + completion calls, ~50% short-turn chat (avg 150 tokens/request) and 50% longer completions (avg 800 tokens/request).
- Expected steady-state monthly volume: you mentioned a starting band of 10M–30M tokens/month, with potential to scale to 100M over 12 months.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for chat flows.

Initial cost guidance (ballpark):
- Redwood hosted unit rate target: $1,250 per 1M tokens (this assumes model variant A, 8-bit quantized, with autoscaling and 20% prefix-cache efficiency).
- Effective per-request example: 150-token chat => ~$0.1875; 800-token completion => ~$1.00.
- For 10M tokens/mo => ~$12,500/mo; 30M => ~$37,500/mo.

Notes/assumptions are captured in the spreadsheet. Key levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and model quantization — we can push unit cost down to ~$950–1,050 per 1M with a dedicated Reserved capacity commitment and some model-variant tuning.

Next steps I propose:
1) You drop your preferred monthly volume (best estimate) in the attached sheet and send back.
2) If the numbers look good, we prepare an invoice estimate + PO-ready breakdown for procurement.
3) We can spin up a 2-week pilot (metered) to validate latency & perf on your real traffic.

I've attached the calculator and a one-page cost breakdown CSV. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up tomorrow to walk through the sheet.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0183

Attachment: acme_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: acme_cost_breakdown.csv (CSV with line-item cost rows)

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <p.natarajan@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Pricing & Invoice Estimate

Thanks Sean — useful summary and thanks for the quick calculator. A few clarifications/answers from our side: 

- Short answer on volumes: we expect 15M tokens/month in Q2 (pilot), scaling to ~60M tokens/month by Q4 if results look good. Our burst days could be 2x baseline.
- Budget: procurement has given a target range of $25k–$50k/month for the next phase (Q2 pilot + ramp). They said anything north of $60k/mo will require executive sign-off.
- Important: we need line-item visibility for embedding vs. generation usage — roughly 70% generation / 30% embeddings by token count.

I'll populate the sheet with the 15M baseline and send over by EOD. Can you also split the estimate by model variant (A vs B) and by deployment type (hosted vs dedicated)? That will help our infra procurement decision.

On procurement timeline: once we have a PO-ready estimate, procurement wants a 2–3 week review before issuing a PO.

Best,
Jordan Ellis
Director, AI Platform | Acme Corp
j.ellis@acmecorp.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <p.natarajan@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Pricing & Invoice Estimate

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply and the context on budget. I've updated the attached acme_cost_breakdown.csv with a split by model variant and deployment (hosted vs dedicated). Quick highlights from the updated model: 

- Hosted (Model A, 8-bit): ~$1,250 per 1M tokens (baseline).
- Hosted (Model B, optimized small variant): ~$1,050 per 1M tokens but with slightly higher p95 latency on long completions.
- Dedicated reserved (Model A): ~$950 per 1M tokens with a 12-month commit and baseline 24/7 capacity — this assumes 40% improvement from batching + cache gains at your expected mix.

Estimated monthly totals (15M tokens, 70% generation / 30% embeddings):
- Hosted Model A: 15 * $1,250 = $18,750/mo (est)
- Hosted Model B: 15 * $1,050 = $15,750/mo (est)
- Dedicated (reserved) Model A: 15 * $950 = $14,250/mo (est)

If your procurement band is $25k–$50k, the hosted options are comfortably inside that range; the dedicated reserved option gives the best unit economics and is closest to the low end of your target once you scale.

I've also attached a PO-ready invoice-style breakdown (line items for tokens, storage, routing, support, and one-time setup). For governance/validation, here's a share link to the detailed cost folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-pricing

Proposed next steps:
- Jordan: confirm the 15M tokens/month baseline in the attached sheet and indicate preferred model/deployment variant by EOD Monday.
- Marissa (cc): once Jordan confirms, can you prepare a procurement-ready PDF and indicate typical lead time for invoicing/contract?
- I'll draft a short SOW for a 2-week pilot (metered) that includes SLA targets and a simple rollback policy.

Happy to jump on 20-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the line items.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_cost_breakdown.csv

Hi Jordan — looping in procurement ops for visibility and next steps. A couple notes from Redwood's side: 

- We can produce a PO-ready PDF and an invoice estimate within 48 hours of your confirmation.
- Billing contact: can you confirm who in Acme will receive invoices and the preferred billing cadence (monthly vs net-30)?
- Trial billing: the 2-week pilot will be metered with a capped exposure so procurement can limit financial risk. We typically invoice pilot usage on the following month, or roll it into the first paid month if a PO is issued.

Jordan, I'll start the PO-ready doc as soon as Sean confirms your selected model/deployment. If procurement prefers a formal quote number for approvals, we can also provide a quote with a 30-day validity window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
